product_context.executive_summary: A local Windows 11 project-execution application that connects Project/Milestone/Task/Subtask planning to 25-minute Pomodoro focus sessions. Users organize actionable work, start a Pomodoro directly from a Task or Subtask, see work context and motivational messages in a compact Always-on-Top window, deliberately handle early-stop friction, and decide after each completed focus interval whether the work item is done, needs a break, or needs another Pomodoro. Progress is calculated from completed actionable leaf work items, while Task/Milestone/Project completion remains an explicit user decision. The MVP is local-only with no login, cloud sync, collaboration, AI, or network dependency.
product_context.problem_statement: A standalone Pomodoro timer records time without connecting focus to concrete project outcomes. The target user needs a lightweight way to break projects into actionable work, focus on one real Task/Subtask at a time, resist premature stopping, preserve effort history, and explicitly close work when it is actually finished without turning the product into a heavyweight project-management suite.
product_context.product_vision: Turn project plans into deliberate, context-rich focus sessions: choose the next actionable work item, focus for 25 minutes, then consciously continue, rest, or mark the work complete.

primary_users.name: Local Windows knowledge worker
primary_users.context: Works on projects on a Windows 11 PC and wants a compact focus companion rather than a collaborative project-management system.
primary_users.jtbd: When I have project work to execute, help me choose a concrete Task/Subtask, stay focused for one Pomodoro, remember why the work matters, and deliberately decide whether it is complete.
pain_points: Standalone Pomodoro sessions lack task context.
Large project-management tools can create overhead.
It is easy to stop a focus interval prematurely.
desired_outcomes: Every focus session is linked to real work.
Project progress reflects completed actionable work.
The timer stays visible without obstructing work.

constraints.text: MVP is local-only and requires no login, cloud, or internet for core operation.
Machine schema lacks a Desktop Application category; Automation Workflow is used only as a schema-compatible routing label and is not the authoritative product category.

mvp: Tasks and optional Subtasks with TODO/IN_PROGRESS/DONE
Optional Why / Desired Outcome on Task/Subtask
25-minute Pomodoro started from Task or Subtask
User-configured Focus and Cancel motivational messages
Manual post-focus choice: Mark Done, Take Break, Start Another Pomodoro
Return to same work context after Break
Immutable MVP Pomodoro history and focused-time summary
Incomplete-child warning with Mark Done Anyway
Local persistence, completion sound setting, sleep/lock-correct timing
Single active Focus or Break timer
post_mvp: Crash/forced-termination session recovery if later approved
Performance optimization after representative workload target is known

user_journeys.title: Create a project and actionable work
user_journeys.trigger: User wants to organize work before focusing.
main_path: Create a Project.
Optionally create one or more Milestones.
Create Tasks under the Project or Milestone.
Optionally create Subtasks under a Task.
Optionally add Why / Desired Outcome to a Task or Subtask.
Project detail shows the hierarchy and calculated progress.
alternative_paths: Skip Milestone and create Tasks directly under Project.
Skip Subtasks and use Task as the actionable leaf item.
failure_paths: Required title is empty and save is rejected.
Persistence fails and the UI reports failure without creating a partial item.
user_journeys.completion_state: At least one actionable Task or Subtask exists and can start a Pomodoro.

user_journeys.title: Start and run a contextual Pomodoro
user_journeys.trigger: User chooses a Task or Subtask and starts focus.
preconditions: Selected work item is not DONE.
No other Focus or Break timer is active.
main_path: User selects Start Pomodoro on a Task or Subtask.
If the work item is TODO, it becomes IN_PROGRESS.
A 25-minute focus session is created and linked to the work item.
Small Always-on-Top focus window appears.
Window shows remaining time, work-item title, optional Why / Desired Outcome, and scrolling motivation.
Remaining time is derived from absolute time boundaries.
alternative_paths: User moves the mini window anywhere on the desktop while it remains Always-on-Top.
failure_paths: A second timer start is rejected while another timer is active.
Local persistence failure prevents the session from starting and is surfaced to the user.
user_journeys.completion_state: Focus session is active and linked to exactly one Task or Subtask.

user_journeys.title: Complete a Pomodoro and choose the next action
user_journeys.trigger: A focus session reaches its 25-minute end time.
main_path: Session result becomes COMPLETED.
Optional completion sound follows the saved setting.
Completion UI asks whether the work item is finished.
User chooses Mark Task/Subtask Done, Take Break, or Start Another Pomodoro.
No work item is auto-completed merely because the focus session completed.
alternative_paths: Mark Done leads to Task completed state with Take Break or Back to Project.
Take Break leaves the work item IN_PROGRESS.
Start Another Pomodoro starts another 25-minute session on the same work item.
failure_paths: If persistence of the completed session fails, completion is not silently lost; an error/retry path is shown.
user_journeys.completion_state: Completed Pomodoro history is preserved and the user's selected next action is respected.

user_journeys.title: Attempt to stop focus early
user_journeys.trigger: User presses Stop/Cancel or closes the focus window before the 25-minute focus session is complete.
preconditions: Focus session is active and remaining time is greater than zero.
main_path: Application displays a motivational confirmation containing current work context.
User may choose Continue Focus or Stop Anyway.
Continue Focus preserves the active session.
Stop Anyway records STOPPED_EARLY and actual focused duration.
The work item remains IN_PROGRESS and is not marked DONE automatically.
alternative_paths: Window-close request uses the same early-stop confirmation.
failure_paths: Closing the confirmation without choosing Stop Anyway leaves the focus session active.
user_journeys.completion_state: Either focus continues or an immutable stopped-early history entry exists.

user_journeys.title: Take a break and return to the same work
user_journeys.trigger: User selects Take Break after focus completion or task completion.
main_path: User starts a 5-minute, 10-minute, or configured custom break.
Break timer stays Always-on-Top.
Break can be stopped at any time without motivational friction.
When break completes, UI identifies the work item from which the break originated.
User chooses Start Another Pomodoro or Back to Project.
alternative_paths: User ends the break early and returns to the project without friction.
failure_paths: A second timer start is rejected while Break is active.
user_journeys.completion_state: User returns to the same work context or project; focus never auto-starts.

user_journeys.title: Complete work hierarchy manually
user_journeys.trigger: User decides a Subtask, Task, Milestone, or Project is actually complete.
main_path: User explicitly invokes Mark Done / Mark Complete.
Task/Subtask becomes DONE only by explicit user action.
Milestone and Project completion are also explicit.
If a parent Task has incomplete Subtasks, a warning appears.
User may Cancel or Mark Done Anyway.
Progress percentage remains calculated from leaf work-item completion, independent of parent completion state.
alternative_paths: A DONE Task/Subtask can be reopened to IN_PROGRESS.
failure_paths: Persistence failure leaves the prior state intact and reports an error.
user_journeys.completion_state: Completion state reflects explicit user confirmation.

user_journeys.title: Delete, archive, and restore while preserving history
user_journeys.trigger: User wants to remove or hide work.
main_path: Items without Pomodoro history may be hard-deleted after confirmation.
Items with Pomodoro history cannot be hard-deleted through the standard UI.
Projects may be archived without deleting child items or history.
Archived projects are excluded from the active list.
User may restore an archived project to ACTIVE.
alternative_paths: User cancels destructive confirmation and no data changes.
failure_paths: Persistence failure prevents partial deletion/archive operations.

functional_requirements.title: Manage Projects
functional_requirements.description: Users can create, view, edit, complete, archive, restore, and conditionally delete Projects. New Projects begin ACTIVE.
functional_requirements.user_value: Provides the top-level container for focused work.
acceptance_criteria: A Project requires a non-empty title after trimming whitespace.
A newly created Project has status ACTIVE.
Editing a Project preserves all child Milestones, Tasks, Subtasks, and Pomodoro history.
Mark Project Complete occurs only after explicit user action; it is never triggered solely by 100% calculated progress.
An archived Project is hidden from the active-project list and remains available in an archived-project view.
Restoring an archived Project returns it to ACTIVE and preserves children/history.
A Project with any descendant Pomodoro history cannot be hard-deleted through the standard UI.

functional_requirements.title: Manage Optional Milestones
functional_requirements.description: Users may create, edit, manually complete, and conditionally delete Milestones inside a Project. Milestones are optional.
functional_requirements.user_value: Supports larger project phases without forcing hierarchy.
acceptance_criteria: A Project can contain zero Milestones.
A Milestone requires a non-empty title.
A Task may exist directly under a Project without a Milestone.
Completing all work inside a Milestone does not automatically complete the Milestone.
When all actionable work under a Milestone is complete, the UI may indicate Ready to complete milestone.
A Milestone with descendant Pomodoro history cannot be hard-deleted through the standard UI.

functional_requirements.title: Manage Tasks
functional_requirements.description: Users can create, view, edit, manually complete, reopen, and conditionally delete Tasks under a Project or Milestone.
functional_requirements.user_value: Creates concrete units of project work.
acceptance_criteria: A Task requires a non-empty title.
A Task may be created directly under a Project or under a Milestone.
A new Task begins TODO.
Starting its first Pomodoro changes TODO to IN_PROGRESS.
Mark Done changes the Task to DONE only through explicit user action.
Reopen changes DONE to IN_PROGRESS.
A Task with Pomodoro history cannot be hard-deleted through the standard UI.

functional_requirements.title: Manage Optional Subtasks
functional_requirements.description: Users may create, edit, manually complete, reopen, and conditionally delete Subtasks under a Task. Subtasks are optional.
functional_requirements.user_value: Allows decomposition without making it mandatory.
acceptance_criteria: A Task can contain zero Subtasks.
A Subtask requires a non-empty title.
A new Subtask begins TODO.
A Subtask can start and own its own Pomodoro sessions.
The parent Task remains eligible to start Pomodoro sessions even when Subtasks exist.
Completing all Subtasks does not automatically mark the parent Task DONE.
A Subtask with Pomodoro history cannot be hard-deleted through the standard UI.

functional_requirements.title: Capture Why / Desired Outcome
functional_requirements.description: Each Task and Subtask may store an optional Why / Desired Outcome text used as focus context.
functional_requirements.user_value: Reminds the user why the current work matters.
acceptance_criteria: Why / Desired Outcome is optional and does not block saving a Task/Subtask.
When present, it is displayed in the work-item detail.
When present, it is available to the active focus window and early-stop confirmation.
When absent, the UI does not fabricate or download replacement content.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce Work-Item Status Transitions
functional_requirements.description: Task/Subtask status is TODO, IN_PROGRESS, or DONE; Pomodoro start and explicit user actions control transitions.
functional_requirements.user_value: Keeps execution state simple and predictable.
acceptance_criteria: New Task/Subtask = TODO.
Starting the first Pomodoro on a TODO item changes it to IN_PROGRESS.
Completing a Pomodoro does not automatically change the work item to DONE.
Only explicit Mark Done changes a Task/Subtask to DONE.
Reopen changes DONE to IN_PROGRESS.
Stopped-early focus leaves the work item IN_PROGRESS.

functional_requirements.title: Calculate Leaf-Based Project Progress
functional_requirements.description: Project progress is the percentage of completed actionable leaf work items; parent Tasks with Subtasks are excluded from the denominator.
functional_requirements.user_value: Prevents double counting and separates work progress from parent completion confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: A Task without Subtasks counts as one progress unit.
A Task with one or more Subtasks does not count as a progress unit; each Subtask counts as one unit.
Milestones and Projects never count as progress units.
Each progress unit has equal weight in MVP.
Progress = DONE leaf units / total leaf units × 100.
Pomodoro count or focused minutes never changes progress percentage.
A Project with zero leaf units shows an empty/not-started progress state rather than presenting a misleading calculated percentage.

functional_requirements.title: Start Pomodoro from Task or Subtask
functional_requirements.description: A 25-minute Focus session can be started only from a selected Task or Subtask and is linked to exactly that work item.
functional_requirements.user_value: Makes every focus session accountable to real project work.
acceptance_criteria: Start Pomodoro is available on eligible Task and Subtask detail.
A new focus session stores exactly one work_item_id.
The work item may be a parent Task even if it has Subtasks.
A DONE work item must be reopened before starting a new Pomodoro.
If any Focus or Break timer is already active, a second timer cannot start.
Focus planned duration is 25 minutes.

functional_requirements.title: Maintain Accurate Focus Time
functional_requirements.description: Focus remaining time is derived from absolute start/end timestamps rather than accumulated UI timer ticks.
functional_requirements.user_value: Ensures lock, sleep, and delayed UI updates do not corrupt focus timing.
acceptance_criteria: At focus start, the system persists a start time and expected end time.
Displayed remaining time is recalculated from the expected end time.
If Windows lock/sleep lasts beyond the expected end time, the session is treated as completed when the application resumes.
UI refresh callbacks are not the authoritative time source.
The session cannot report negative remaining time.

functional_requirements.title: Provide Small Movable Always-on-Top Focus Window
functional_requirements.description: During Focus and Break, a compact window remains Always-on-Top and can be moved anywhere on the Windows desktop.
functional_requirements.user_value: Keeps time/context visible without taking over the workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Starting Focus opens or activates the compact timer window.
The timer window is Always-on-Top while Focus or Break is active.
User can drag the window to another desktop location without stopping the timer.
Focus window shows remaining time and work-item title.
If Why / Desired Outcome exists, it can be shown as contextual text.
Closing the window during incomplete Focus routes through FR-012 rather than silently terminating the session.

functional_requirements.title: Configure and Scroll Motivational Messages
functional_requirements.description: Users can manage local Focus motivational messages and early-cancel motivational messages; Focus messages scroll/rotate below the timer.
functional_requirements.user_value: Maintains the original motivational behavior inside task-context focus.
acceptance_criteria: Setup provides separate collections for Focus Messages and Cancel Messages.
Users can add, edit, and remove their own messages.
Saved messages persist across application restarts.
During active Focus, available Focus Messages are displayed in a scrolling/rotating area below the timer.
When the Focus Message list is empty, focus still works and no unapproved default/network content is generated.

functional_requirements.title: Apply Friction to Early Focus Stop
functional_requirements.description: Stopping or closing an incomplete Focus session requires a motivational confirmation with Continue Focus and Stop Anyway.
functional_requirements.user_value: Creates deliberate friction against giving up while preserving user control.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing Stop before focus end displays the confirmation.
Closing the focus window before focus end displays the same confirmation.
Confirmation identifies the active work-item title and may show Why / Desired Outcome and a configured Cancel Message.
Continue Focus dismisses the confirmation and preserves the same active session/end time.
Stop Anyway ends the session with result STOPPED_EARLY and does not mark the work item DONE.
No forced waiting period is required before Stop Anyway.

functional_requirements.title: Ask What Happens After Focus Completion
functional_requirements.description: When Focus reaches 25 minutes, the user chooses Mark Task/Subtask Done, Take Break, or Start Another Pomodoro.
functional_requirements.user_value: Separates completion of a focus interval from completion of the underlying work.
acceptance_criteria: At expected end time the session result becomes COMPLETED.
The work item is not auto-marked DONE.
Completion UI offers Mark Done, Take Break, and Start Another Pomodoro.
Start Another Pomodoro creates a new separate 25-minute session on the same work item.
After Focus completion the user may close/leave without early-stop friction.

functional_requirements.title: Run Configurable Manual Breaks
functional_requirements.description: Breaks are started manually, use 5-minute, 10-minute, or configured custom duration, remain Always-on-Top, and can be stopped without friction.
functional_requirements.user_value: Supports recovery without forcing the user into or out of work.
acceptance_criteria: Break never starts automatically after Focus.
Setup allows 5-minute, 10-minute, or a valid custom break duration.
User explicitly starts Break.
Break timer remains Always-on-Top.
User can stop Break at any time without motivational confirmation.
Focus does not auto-start when Break completes.

functional_requirements.title: Return to the Same Work Context After Break
functional_requirements.description: A break retains the originating Task/Subtask context so the user can continue the same work or return to Project.
functional_requirements.user_value: Reduces context switching between focus intervals.
acceptance_criteria: A Break started from a Focus completion stores the originating work-item reference.
At Break completion, the UI identifies that originating work item.
Actions are Start Another Pomodoro and Back to Project.
Start Another Pomodoro targets the same originating work item.
No next work item is selected automatically.

functional_requirements.title: Preserve Pomodoro History
functional_requirements.description: Every ended Focus session is stored as immutable MVP history linked to the originating work item and Project.
functional_requirements.user_value: Provides a trustworthy effort record without using it as completion progress.
acceptance_criteria: History stores work item, Project, start time, end time, planned duration, actual focused duration, and result.
Supported result values are COMPLETED and STOPPED_EARLY.
History records whether the work item was marked DONE as the immediate post-session action when applicable.
History is viewable from the work item.
History is not editable through the MVP UI.
Pomodoro count and focused minutes are summaries of history and do not modify project progress.

functional_requirements.title: Complete Tasks/Subtasks Manually with Child Warning
functional_requirements.description: Task/Subtask completion is explicit; marking a parent Task DONE while any Subtask is incomplete requires a warning but remains allowed.
functional_requirements.user_value: Preserves user judgment while preventing accidental closure of unfinished child work.
acceptance_criteria: Mark Done requires an explicit user action.
If a Task has no incomplete Subtasks, Mark Done changes it to DONE.
If one or more Subtasks are not DONE, the UI reports the number of incomplete Subtasks and offers Cancel and Mark Done Anyway.
Cancel preserves the prior Task status.
Mark Done Anyway sets the parent Task to DONE without changing child Subtask statuses.
Completing a Subtask never auto-completes its parent Task.

functional_requirements.title: Complete Milestones Manually
functional_requirements.description: Milestones are completed only by explicit user confirmation.
functional_requirements.user_value: Allows phase review even after all underlying actionable work is done.
acceptance_criteria: Completing all leaf work under a Milestone does not change Milestone completion automatically.
When all actionable work under a Milestone is DONE, the UI may indicate Ready to complete milestone.
Explicit Mark Milestone Complete changes its completion state.
Milestone completion does not change Task/Subtask statuses.

functional_requirements.title: Complete Projects Manually
functional_requirements.description: Projects are completed only by explicit user confirmation, independent of calculated progress.
functional_requirements.user_value: Ensures project closure reflects user judgment rather than arithmetic alone.
acceptance_criteria: A Project reaching 100% leaf progress is not auto-completed.
At 100% progress the UI may indicate All project tasks completed / Ready to complete.
Explicit Mark Project Complete changes status to COMPLETED.
Completing a Project preserves the full hierarchy and Pomodoro history.

functional_requirements.title: Protect History During Deletion
functional_requirements.description: Hard deletion through the standard UI is allowed only when the target item and its descendants have no Pomodoro history.
functional_requirements.user_value: Prevents orphaned or misleading focus history.
acceptance_criteria: Delete requires confirmation.
An item with no own or descendant Pomodoro history may be hard-deleted.
An item with own or descendant Pomodoro history cannot be hard-deleted through standard UI.
Rejected deletion leaves the hierarchy and history unchanged.
Cancelling delete leaves data unchanged.

functional_requirements.title: Archive and Restore Projects
functional_requirements.description: Projects can be archived and restored while preserving all hierarchy and history.
functional_requirements.user_value: Keeps inactive work out of the active list without destroying records.
acceptance_criteria: Archive removes the Project from the active-project list.
Archive preserves Milestones, Tasks, Subtasks, Why text, and Pomodoro history.
Archived Project appears in an archived-project view/list.
Restore returns the Project to ACTIVE.
Restore does not alter child status or history.

functional_requirements.title: Persist MVP Data Locally
functional_requirements.description: Projects, hierarchy, settings, messages, timer state needed for lock/sleep correctness, and history are stored locally on the Windows device.
functional_requirements.user_value: Allows the application to work without accounts, cloud, or internet.
acceptance_criteria: Core workflows function with the device offline.
No login is required.
Project/work-item data and settings remain after normal application restart.
No third-party network service is required for MVP operation.
The implementation must not add cloud sync or telemetry as an unstated MVP dependency.

functional_requirements.title: Configure Completion Sound
functional_requirements.description: Users can enable or disable a local sound when a Focus session completes.
functional_requirements.user_value: Provides completion feedback without making sound mandatory.
acceptance_criteria: Setup exposes completion sound On/Off.
The setting persists locally.
When On, a Focus completion produces the configured application completion sound behavior.
When Off, Focus completion is silent.
Stopped-early Focus does not trigger Focus-complete sound.

functional_requirements.title: Allow Only One Active Timer
functional_requirements.description: The application permits at most one active Focus or Break timer at a time.
functional_requirements.user_value: Prevents ambiguous session ownership and timing.
acceptance_criteria: Starting Focus while Focus or Break is active is rejected.
Starting Break while Focus or Break is active is rejected.
After the active timer ends or is explicitly stopped, a new timer can start.
The UI clearly identifies the currently active timer type and associated work item where applicable.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The MVP shall run as a Windows 11 desktop application using the confirmed C# + .NET 10 + WPF stack.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Build and manual smoke test on supported Windows 11 environment

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Timer correctness shall be based on absolute time boundaries so delayed UI callbacks, lock, or sleep do not extend the planned Focus interval.
non_functional_requirements.target: No authoritative timing from tick accumulation
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Unit tests with injected clock plus lock/sleep manual validation

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Core MVP operation shall not require transmitting project, task, motivational-message, or Pomodoro-history data to a remote service.
non_functional_requirements.target: 0 required remote data transfers for core MVP

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Local write operations shall avoid intentionally leaving partial hierarchy/session records when a save operation fails.
non_functional_requirements.target: Atomic/transactional behavior where multiple persisted records must change together; exact storage mechanism is implementation-defined

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Project-detail and history UI performance shall have an explicit benchmark before optimization claims are made.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Define benchmark fixtures before performance acceptance testing

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Timer calculation, project hierarchy/progress calculation, persistence, and WPF presentation logic should be separable enough to unit-test domain behavior without driving the UI.
non_functional_requirements.target: Domain timer/progress rules covered by automated unit tests

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Primary controls shall be usable with keyboard navigation and shall expose meaningful accessible names where supported by WPF.
non_functional_requirements.target: Keyboard path for create/edit/start/stop/complete/break flows; exact WCAG conformance level UNSPECIFIED

data_requirements.sensitivity: Local productivity data; no regulated classification confirmed
data_requirements.lifecycle: Create/edit; manual complete; archive/restore; hard delete only if no descendant history

data_requirements.description: Concrete work item under Project or Milestone.
validation: milestone when set must belong to same Project

data_requirements.description: Optional child work item under Task.
Immutable-ended focus history linked to exactly one Task or Subtask.
validation: planned focus duration 25 minutes for MVP
data_requirements.lifecycle: Created at focus start; finalized on complete/early stop; ended history not editable in MVP UI

data_requirements.description: Temporary/local break timing state retaining originating work-item context when applicable.
validation: duration must be a valid configured break duration
data_requirements.lifecycle: Created on explicit Start Break; finalized on completion/early stop

data_requirements.description: Local Pomodoro and UI behavior settings.
validation: custom break duration must be positive; exact maximum UNSPECIFIED
data_requirements.sensitivity: Local user preferences and free-text motivation
data_requirements.lifecycle: Persist until user edits/removes or app data is deleted

roles_permissions.capability: Read/create/update local projects, milestones, tasks, subtasks and settings
roles_permissions.conditions: Single local-user MVP; no account or role system.

roles_permissions.capability: Hard-delete item with no own/descendant Pomodoro history
Hard-delete item with own/descendant Pomodoro history
roles_permissions.conditions: Use non-destructive project archive where applicable.

security_privacy.text: No authentication is required for the confirmed single-local-user MVP.
Core MVP must not require sending project/task/motivation/history data to third-party services.
Validate free-text titles/messages and persisted data safely; do not treat stored text as executable instructions/code.
Do not store secrets because no remote integration is approved for MVP.
Do not add telemetry or third-party network SDKs as unstated MVP dependencies.

analytics_observability.text: MVP product analytics are local-only; no remote analytics service is approved.
Operational errors should be diagnosable without logging unnecessary user free-text content.
Pomodoro history is product data, not remote telemetry.

testing.intent: Validate leaf-work-item project progress including parent Tasks with Subtasks and zero-leaf projects.
Validate Task/Subtask status transitions and no automatic DONE on Pomodoro completion.
Validate absolute-time timer behavior with normal passage, delayed callbacks, lock/sleep simulation, and overdue resume.
Validate Pomodoro start/finalization persistence and immutable completed/stopped-early history.
Validate Always-on-Top focus window, draggable behavior, context display, and early-stop confirmation via Stop and Close.
Validate completion choices: Mark Done, Take Break, and Start Another Pomodoro without auto-completion.
Validate 5/10/custom manual break, frictionless break stop, same-work return, and no auto-started focus.
Validate delete protection when own/descendant history exists and archive/restore preservation.
Validate local persistence of Projects, hierarchy, Why text, motivation messages, settings, and history across restart.
Validate incomplete-subtask warning and Mark Done Anyway without altering child statuses.
Validate core project/focus/break/history workflows without network access or login.
Validate expected Focus completion after Windows 11 lock/sleep exceeds remaining focus time.

release_criteria: All MVP FR acceptance criteria pass.
All blocking questions remain resolved; non-blocking questions are documented.
Windows 11 Always-on-Top, drag, early-stop, sound, break, and lock/sleep manual tests pass.
Offline core-flow test passes without login/network.
Delete protection and archive/restore preserve history.
Coding agent reports any deviation from this PRD; no unapproved feature/technology is introduced.

risks.description: Progress can become misleading if parent Tasks and Subtasks are double-counted.
risks.mitigation: Use the confirmed leaf-work-item algorithm and automated fixtures.
risks.contingency: Disable/revert progress display if reconciliation tests fail.

risks.description: UI timer tick accumulation can make sessions inaccurate across sleep/lock or delayed rendering.
risks.mitigation: Use persisted absolute start/expected-end timestamps; UI callbacks only refresh display.
risks.contingency: Reconcile active session against current clock on resume/activation.

risks.description: Deleting work items with focus history can orphan or misrepresent historical effort.
risks.mitigation: Block standard hard-delete when own/descendant Pomodoro history exists; archive Projects instead.
risks.contingency: Preserve records and expose a non-destructive archive path.

risks.description: A parent Task can be marked DONE while child Subtasks remain incomplete, creating intentionally inconsistent-looking states.
risks.mitigation: Show count-aware warning and require Mark Done Anyway confirmation; do not silently mutate child status.

risks.description: Unknown expected project/history volume means UI performance targets cannot yet be objectively certified.
risks.mitigation: Keep target UNSPECIFIED and add benchmark fixtures before performance claims.
risks.contingency: Profile and optimize after representative volume is known.

risks.description: Unexpected process termination can leave an active session requiring reconciliation on next launch.
risks.mitigation: Persist enough active timer boundary state for lock/sleep correctness; crash-recovery UX is explicitly not an approved MVP feature.
risks.contingency: Report unresolved active session behavior as a known limitation rather than inventing recovery semantics.

assumptions.text: Focus time continues according to wall-clock time while Windows is locked or sleeping.
assumptions.risk: None remaining for product semantics; implementation must preserve it.
assumptions.validation_method: Automated injected-clock tests plus Windows 11 lock/sleep manual test.

assumptions.text: Only one Focus or Break timer may be active at any time.
A Project with zero actionable leaf work items uses an empty/not-started progress state rather than a misleading calculated percentage.
assumptions.rationale: Needed to make the confirmed progress formula defined for an empty denominator.
assumptions.risk: Low; exact visual treatment remains design-level.

assumptions.text: Moving an existing Task between compatible Milestones/Projects, if implemented, must preserve the Task identity and its historical sessions.
assumptions.rationale: History should remain attached to the work performed, not to a newly created replacement record.
assumptions.risk: Move functionality itself is not explicitly required in MVP; agent must not add it unless needed/approved.
assumptions.validation_method: Do not implement move behavior unless separately approved; if added, preserve IDs/history.

assumptions.text: Normal process crash/forced termination does not have a user-confirmed auto-resume/recovery flow in MVP.
assumptions.rationale: Crash recovery was not approved as product behavior.
assumptions.risk: An interrupted active session may need conservative handling or be documented as a limitation.
assumptions.validation_method: Agent must surface any needed decision instead of inventing recovery UX.

open_questions.question: What is the final product name?
open_questions.impact: Branding only; does not block implementation of product behavior.

open_questions.question: What installer/distribution format should be used for the first release?
open_questions.impact: Affects packaging/release pipeline, not core application behavior.

open_questions.question: What representative maximum Project/Task/Subtask/Pomodoro-history volume should define performance benchmarks?
open_questions.impact: Needed to replace NFR-005 UNSPECIFIED with measurable UI-performance targets.

open_questions.question: Should crash/forced-termination session recovery become a future approved feature?
open_questions.impact: Would define next-launch reconciliation UX for interrupted active timers.

open_questions.question: Should custom break duration have a product-level maximum?
open_questions.impact: Validation boundary is currently implementation-defined except that the value must be positive.

coding_agent_handoff.repository_status: Unknown; inspect before naming files/paths or selecting a local persistence library.
